name: draft-paper-reviewer
description: TeX-only draft paper review and revision workflow for Codex with local related-paper downloads, downloaded-paper convention mining, figure/table retention gates, formula-symbol first-use checks, material reports, term usage auditing, paired reviewer/reviser loops, XLSX revision ledgers, fixed numbered reports, and a 99 ultimate summary.

interface.shortDescription: Run a literature-evidence-driven manuscript review and revision workflow.
interface.longDescription: Installs repo-local Codex custom agents for an iterative draft-paper review workflow. The submitted manuscript input is TeX-only: Stage 0 accepts a TeX source directory or explicit .tex root file, rejects PDF/Word/Markdown/plain-text/image manuscripts, and confirms all parameters with defaults before any ingestion, literature search, review, or revision. The workflow serves the user's own manuscript-development process, handles incomplete experiments/tables as local result-claim constraints rather than blanket contribution weakness, discovers related literature by topic group and citation rank, downloads public related-paper artifacts according to the confirmed all/top-X/required-only/no-download policy, mines downloaded local papers for section-level writing, terminology, formula-notation, experiment, table, and figure conventions, then builds an evidence map. A figure/table retention gate decides whether existing evidence artifacts must be kept, revised, moved, merged, or may be deleted before any TeX revision. The workflow runs material reviewer and specialist audits, synthesizes scores, plans revisions, then revises copied TeX files through one-to-one reviewer/reviser pairs. Literature is used both for evidence and for downloaded-paper writing calibration, including contribution framing, method exposition, formula-symbol explanation patterns, experiment/table/figure narration, limitations, and field-standard term usage. A dedicated term-usage auditor checks nouns, formula symbols, acronyms, method names, dataset names, metrics, and proper nouns for internal and downloaded-literature-aligned consistency; symbols must be needed at first occurrence and explained at or before first use. Report materiality gating writes standalone reports only for author-relevant, principle-level, verification/comparison, or high-impact writing risks while preserving fixed report numbers and leaving absent numbers undocumented. Each paired review/write round is logged to JSONL and exported to an XLSX workbook with one sheet per pair, with CSV fallback exports. Stage 17 writes 99_ultimate_summary.md as the final first-read report. Objective limitations such as missing experiments or unavailable raw data can be deferred after repeated attempts, and writing guidance is used for narrative, citation, reproducibility, limitations, style, dataset-setting, and venue-checklist revisions.

Review the TeX source in this repository.

Run evidence-based peer review and produce a revision plan.

Check whether my paper's figures and tables can be deleted or must be kept before revising.
Review my TeX draft, audit term usage, and produce numbered reports ending with 99_ultimate_summary.md.
Review my TeX draft and check formula symbols are explained before first use.
